paper.title: Food Image Recognition by Using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)

summarization.summary: This study addresses food image recognition using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) on a dataset of 5,822 RGB images. The primary contribution is demonstrating that data augmentation via affine transformations effectively mitigates severe overfitting in small-scale datasets, raising test accuracy from 74% to 90%, which significantly outperforms the Bag-of-Features baseline at 56%. The methodology employed a five-layer CNN trained for 400 epochs, achieving an overall accuracy of 90% with category-specific rates ranging from 67% to 98%. However, documented limitations include the small dataset size, which necessitated augmentation and prevented further gains beyond 400 epochs without risking overtraining. The authors explicitly state that manual image collection is critical for future improvements rather than relying solely on augmentation or transfer learning. While the paper focuses specifically on food images, these findings regarding data scarcity and augmentation strategies are relevant to general CNN image recognition tasks facing similar dataset constraints.
